findings.title: Convert the legacy OTP model before exposing it as a federated credential
findings.body: The new getCredentials implementation returns myUser.otp directly, but updateCredential stores that model with the input type (`totp` or `hotp`), not the credential-provider type `otp`. Previously this provider exposed OTP through getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, which reports `otp`. Returning the legacy model changes the advertised credential type and breaks consumers such as the existing account REST test, which looks for the credential under `OTPCredentialModel.TYPE`. Expose a correctly converted OTPCredentialModel while preserving the stored credential ID.

findings.title: Exercise consumption of federated recovery codes, not just successful validation
findings.body: The recovery-code validator accepts any generated code without consuming it, and getCredentials reconstructs a fresh model with every code unused on each call. Consequently, repeated logins can reuse the same code indefinitely, the form always requests the first code, and the authenticator's exhaustion/regeneration path is never exercised. The new integration test stops after one login, so it passes with this invalid recovery-code lifecycle. Persist consumption in the test provider and extend the test to check replay rejection, the next requested code, and regeneration after exhaustion.
